// The query could detect automated data exfiltration attempts by monitoring suspicious IP addresses.",,,,"# Microsoft Graph API Attacks Using UEBA Threat Intelligence
displayName: ""Microsoft Graph API Attacks Detected via UEBA Threat Intelligence""
Detects Microsoft Graph API attacks by correlating UEBA threat intelligence data with Graph API activity logs.
This detection identifies when IP addresses flagged by threat intelligence as ""AttackerIP"" are making calls to
Microsoft Graph APIs against the Entra tenant. The rule leverages Sentinel UEBA behavioral analytics to
triangulate attackers launching Graph API attacks, providing early warning of potential data exfiltration,
reconnaissance, or privilege escalation attempts. This correlation helps identify sophisticated attacks that
may bypass traditional security controls by using legitimate Graph API endpoints with malicious intent.

// DNS tunneling is a method used by threat actors to encode non-DNS traffic within DNS packets. This technique allows data to bypass traditional network firewalls, creating covert channels for data exfiltration and infiltration. By centralizing your enterprise DNS logging and utilizing Microsoft Sentinel SIEM, you can leverage my Sentinel KQL (DnsEvents Schema) to hunt for DNS tunneling activities.
